How do Buatsi and Hutchinson's records compare?

Buatsi and Hutchinson made their professional debuts just three months apart in 2017 and have amassed strikingly similar records.

After catching the eye by winning bronze for Team GB at the 2016 Olympics, Buatsi won his first 19 fights in the professional ranks, collecting 13 victories by knockout.

He won the WBO interim light-heavyweight title with a split-decision win over Hutchinson before suffering his one and only defeat against Smith in February 2025.

A majority-decision victory over Parker in November 2025 improved Buatsi's record to 20-1 and put him back on track to challenge for a world title.

Hutchinson enjoyed a 13-fight win streak to begin his professional career but fell to a first defeat when facing Lennox Clarke for the vacant British and Commonwealth super-middleweight titles in 2021.

He rebuilt with five successive victories before losing to Buatsi on the undercard of Daniel Dubois v Anthony Joshua at Wembley.

Following victories over Mark Jeffers and Ezra Taylor, Hutchinson holds a record of 20 wins and two defeats, earning 14 of those by stoppage.

What belts are on the line in Buatsi v Hutchinson 2?

Buatsi and Hutchinson fight for the WBC light-heavyweight belt after American David Benavidez moved up to cruiserweight and vacated.

Russia's Dmitry Bivol is the WBA, WBO and IBF light-heavyweight champion and puts those three belts on the line against Briton Callum Smith in Yekaterinburg on 12 December.

The first fight took place on the undercard of Dubois' stunning stoppage win over Joshua to retain his IBF heavyweight title at Wembley Stadium in September 2025.

Buatsi and Hutchinson set the tone for a fine night of boxing at the national stadium - meeting in the middle and refusing to take a step back.

Hutchinson started strongly but suffered a cut to the side of his right eye following a clash of heads in the fifth round.

Buatsi scored his first of two knockdowns in round six, landing a clean right, before Hutchinson was deducted a point in the seventh for use of the head.

Trailing on the scorecards, Hutchinson threw caution to the wind but went down again in the ninth following a body shot.

Hutchinson beat the count and made it to the final bell with one judge scoring it 113-112 in his favour, but the other two judges' cards read 117–108 and 115–110 for Buatsi.

Buatsi landed 264 of the 600 punches he threw, with 191 of 380 power punches finding their target.

Hutchinson had a slightly lower output with 209 of 566 punches landing and 157 of his attempted 385 power punches connecting.

Billam-Smith and Clarke first met as amateurs in 2016 with the latter coming out on top in the ABA Championships final.

Jamaican-born Briton Clarke went on to enjoy further success as an amateur, winning a silver medal at the 2017 European Championships and claiming bronze at the Commonwealth Games in 2018.

Clarke, 35, also represented Team GB at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021 but did not take home a medal and turned professional in 2022.

He won his first 10 professional contests, stopping seven opponents along the way, and earning the British cruiserweight title, but fell to his first loss against Leonardo Mosquea in 2024.

Clarke lost the British title in his next bout when he ended up on the wrong side of a decision against Viddal Riley.

Back-to-back victories have breathed new life into Clarke's career since, taking his record to 12 wins and two defeats, but Billam-Smith looks set to pose a stern test.

Billam-Smith also has two losses on his professional record - winning 22 of his 24 contests - but has competed at a higher level.

The 36-year-old reigned as European and Commonwealth champion before beating Lawrence Okolie to become WBO cruiserweight world champion in 2023.

He made two successful defences, including victory over Richard Riakporhe - who he had lost to in 2019 - but lost the title to Gilberto Ramirez when attempting to unify in 2024.

Billam-Smith, who has ambitions to return to world level, has won his last two fights.

articles.title: Jake Paul to fight kickboxing champion Cedric Doumbe on Christmas Eve as YouTuber's opponent is revealed
articles.summary: Jake Paul will make his boxing return on Christmas Eve in Dubai, 12 months on from having his jaw broken by Anthony Joshua; former two-time world champion kickboxer turned MMA fighter Cedric Doumbe confirmed as his opponent
articles.body:
It's Paul's first fight since he took on former two-time unified heavyweight world champion Anthony Joshua, where he suffered a broken jaw from a sixth-round knockout blow.

Back in 2024, the YouTuber turned boxer also fought a then-58-year-old Mike Tyson and has a record of 12-2, with seven KOs, since making his professional debut.

His other loss came against Tommy Fury in 2023.

Doumbe is a former two-time welterweight world champion in kickboxing, with a 75-7-1 record including 45 knockouts. The 34-year-old has since transitioned to MMA, recording six KO victories in his first seven professional bouts.

His explosive, nine-second knockout of Jordan Zebo in September 2023 in Paris - witnessed by French football superstar Kylian Mbappe, among others - helped to cement his reputation.

The Cameroon-born Frenchman has one prior fight in professional boxing, beating Mohamed Fodil on points following a four-round bout in 2015.

His meeting with Paul will be a professionally-sanctioned eight-round cruiserweight clash, contested at 200lbs with 10oz gloves.

Paul said upon the announcement of his opponent: "Cedric [Doumbe] was calling me out two years ago after knocking some dude [Zebo] out in nine seconds. Well, now you get your chance.

"I'm rusty, my jaw is janky and I don't have kickboxing world titles like you do. But guess what, this isn't kickboxing mon ami. This is BOXING.

"Just like [Oleksandr] Usyk feasted on Rico Verhoeven, I am going to eat you for dinner in Dubai on Christmas Eve."

Doumbe said: "Jake Paul calls himself the Problem Child, but he's never faced a problem like me.

"Jake loves to talk, and so do I, but after what Joshua did to his jaw, I'm not sure how much talking he has left.

"I'm going to finish the job Joshua started."

articles.title: Conor McGregor confirma que su próxima pelea será la última en la UFC
articles.standfirst: El peleador irlandés puso un tuit en el que sacó pecho por los números que consigue cada vez que sube al octágono, y reveló que no renovará su contrato con la compañía
articles.summary: El peleador irlandés puso un tuit en el que sacó pecho por los números que consigue cada vez que sube al octágono, y reveló que no renovará su contrato con la compañía
articles.body: Conor McGregor ha vuelto a dar que hablar este fin de semana, ya que ha confirmado de una vez por todas que su siguiente pelea en la UFC será la última, ya que no le quedan más en el contrato y no piensa renovarlo. A través de un tuit, 'The Notorious' ha sacado pecho de los números que consigue en cada combate que protagoniza, comparándose con Saúl 'Canelo' Álvarez y afirmando que una vez se recupere de su lesión de ligamento cruzado realizará un 'The Last Dance'. El pasado julio, McGregor regresó al octágono para medirse a Max Holloway en peso wélter después de cinco años de inactividad. El hype era máximo a pesar de que la mayoría consideraban que Conor estaba lejos de su prime, pero todo saltó por los aires cuando en la primera patada que intentó pisó mal y se lesionó de gravedad los ligamentos. Lejos de venirse abajo, el peleador irlandés prometió volver más fuerte en 2027, algo en lo que ha vuelto a incidir demostrando que su intención es despedirse de la UFC con un combate muy diferente al anterior. "¿Cuántas visualizaciones tuvo la pelea de Canelo? ¿Cuántos asistentes hubo? ¿A cuánto ascendió la recaudación en taquilla? ¡Vaya! En cuanto a ventas, supero a todos ellos. Por mucho. A todos y cada uno. Sin despeinarme. Quizás incluso a todos juntos. Y eso que ni siquiera me esfuerzo", escribió McGregor. De hecho, Conor fue más allá, y finalizó su mensaje reconociendo que "mi pelea coincidió con la semifinal de la Copa del Mundo y, aun así, logré esas cifras en ese último combate —una auténtica basura, por cierto—, con el que tendré que cargar durante unos meses más antes de volver. Para mi próxima pelea —mi última pelea—, voy a esforzarme de verdad en la promoción. A ver qué cifras puedo generar. Seguiré superando mis propios récords". Todavía es una incógnita cuándo volverá a pelear McGregor, pero su intención es regresar en verano en la International Fight Week de junio. Según ha mostrado él mismo en varios vídeos, la recuperación va viento en popa, ha dejado atrás sus malos hábitos y se está tomando muy en serio lo que será su última gran aparición en la compañía dirigida por Dana White. Conor fue objeto de críticas tras su última actuación. Se habló de que la lesión vino por la vida tan loca que había tenido los últimos años, que incluso había acudido lesionado a la pelea para cobrar el cheque, que se debería retirar... Todo esto le ha importado poco o nada al irlandés, que se ha encerrado en su búnker de Irlanda y solo quiere acallar todas estas críticas con una última gran actuación. Eso sí, su rival sigue siendo una incógnita. Una trilogía con Max Holloway, una trilogía con Nate Díaz, cualquier otro rival del peso wélter... Muchas dudas y pocos nombres para poner de compañero de baile a 'The Notorious', que obviamente quiere medirse a un nombre mediático para poner el broche de oro y batir todos los récords de ventas posibles después de una carrera que le ha consagrado como el hombre que cambio el deporte y el peleador más mediático de la historia de las MMA.

articles.title: Boxing: Jake Paul to fight MMA and kickboxing star Cedric Doumbe on 24 December
articles.summary: MMA and kickboxing star Cedric Doumbe will welcome Jake Paul back to the boxing ring on 24 December in Dubai.
articles.body:
Jake Paul has announced he will fight MMA star Cedric Doumbe on 24 December in Dubai.

The bout will be Paul's first fight since losing to former British heavyweight champion Anthony Joshua last December.

American Paul had to have two titanium plates fitted and some teeth removed after Joshua broke his jaw during the contest.

The 29-year-old influencer said in May that his boxing career was "most definitely" in doubt following the injury, but he will now return to action on Christmas Eve.

The event, which will take place at the Coca-Cola Arena, will be a professionally sanctioned eight-round cruiserweight bout with the fighters using 10oz gloves.

Cameroonian-born Frenchman Doumbe is a multi-time kickboxing world champion-turned MMA fighter.

The 34-year-old is signed to the Professional Fighters League (PFL) - an MMA promotion that Paul's Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) merged with in July.

He has won two of his three fights since joining the PFL in 2023, but has only one professional boxing bout to his name, which he won in 2015.

Paul has won 12 of his 14 fights as a professional, with his two defeats coming against Tommy Fury and Joshua.

In July 2025, Paul earned a place in the WBA's cruiserweight rankings after beating former world champion Julio Cesar Chavez Jr, but he lost that ranking in January after defeat by Joshua.

Paul was knocked down twice against the British two-time heavyweight world champion before being stopped in the sixth round.

Jake Paul went in a surprising direction for his next opponent for his return fight next month.

After Paul announced last week that he would be fighting on Christmas Eve in Dubai following last December's knockout loss to Anthony Joshua, Most Valuable Promotions announced on Monday that the 29-year-old will face Cedric Doumbé in an eight-round cruiserweight match in his comeback to the ring.

Helwani noted that Doumbé hasn't fought professionally since his last MMA win in May 2024 because he "quietly left competition to focus on family and other personal matters." A veteran kickboxer with a 63-7-1 record, he fought just one boxing match in April 2015.

Doumbé being tabbed as Paul's next opponent is a bit of a shocker after Paul previously called out a long list of potential targets, including Conor McGregor, Canelo Alvarez, Francis Ngannou, Deontay Wilder and Nate Diaz. While he's long faced criticism for cherry-picking his opponents, Paul made it clear that he's excited for his first fight since suffering a broken jaw in his loss to Joshua last year.

"Cédric Douchebag was calling me out two years ago after knocking some dude out in 9 seconds. Well Douchebag, now you get your chance," Paul said in a release. "I'm rusty, my jaw is janky and I don't have kickboxing world titles like you do. But guess what, this isn't kickboxing mon ami. This is BOXING."

Doumbé responded: "Jake Paul calls himself the Problem Child, but he's never faced a problem like me. He has no idea what a Frenchman is capable of, and on Thursday, December 24 in Dubai, I'm going to eat 'El Poulet' for dinner. Jake loves to talk, and so do I, but after what Joshua did to his jaw, I'm not sure how much talking he has left. I'm going to finish the job Joshua started."

articles.body:
Both Billam-Smith and Clarke are coming off victories in thrilling bouts last time out. Billam-Smith came through a bruising battle with the ferocious Ryan Rozicki in June, while Clarke rose from the canvas twice to take out Jack Massey on the same bill.

Clarke, who raced to winning the British title in nine fight, is looking to take his career to a new level.

Billam-Smith is a former world champion, seeking to return to the summit of the division. But he also has a score to settle with Clarke. The man from Gravesend handed him a painful amateur defeat in the final of the 2016 national elite championships and Billam-Smith wants his revenge.

Billam-Smith and Clarke will collide on Saturday November 7, live on Sky Sports.

Live coverage of the action-packed bill in London starts at 7pm on Sky Sports .

Preliminary bouts will be streamed on Sky's digital platforms from 5pm.

Where is the Billam-Smith vs Clarke fight?

Zuffa Boxing 12 takes place at the Copper Box Arena in London.

Billam-Smith has a 22-2 (14) record. He has only been beaten by Richard Riakporhe, a loss which he later avenged, and then WBA world champion Gilberto Ramirez. As well as Riakporhe, he's beaten the likes of Lawrence Okolie, Brandon Glanton and Ryan Rozicki.

Clarke is 12-2 (9). A former British champion and European title challenger, Clarke is coming off a thrilling victory over Jack Massey, a former European champion and previous world title challenger.

Billam-Smith said: "He still carries his power, is fast, got power in all his shots.

"Cheavon isn't as intense as Rozicki - I'm not sure that anyone is - in terms of the way he fights. But he carries much more speed, which adds more danger.

"He puts his shots together well, so that makes him threatening for sure.

"I've sparred him as well. He's no mug. He knows what he's doing in there, he's always super-fit. He's been hurt in the past, he comes back, looks the part. Never been stopped, he might have been dropped but never been stopped.

"It's a hard night's work, I've got to be 100 per cent for it."

Clarke said: "The bull's always driven - but they get tamed. He'll come out with his tactics and everyone has a plan until they get in the ring. On the night we'll see.

"He's a former world champion so you have to give credit where it's due. But regardless I know what my ability is, I've been given a gift. It's wrong for me not to fulfil that gift. So come November 7 we will see."

London's Denzel Bentley fights Shane Mosley Jr, son of boxing legend Shane Mosley, in a world-class middleweight clash.

American heavyweight destroyer Da'Mazion Vanhouter will face Ivan Balaz. Vanhouter had an eye-opening performance on the Garcia vs Benn card in September, demolishing Raphael Akpejiori in the first round.

Scottish middleweight phenom Sam Hickey boxes Amaury Massenaux, while Kayla Allen has her second professional fight against Julia Igel.

Rising cruiserweight Lucas Roehrig will fight Scottish champion Connal McDonald in an eight-rounder.

In the streamed preliminary bouts British light-heavyweight contender Zach Parker will face unbeaten puncher Umar Dzambekov, plus Masood Abdulah fights 14-1 American contender Adan Palma and Vinnie "King of Violence" Kemp makes his pro debut.

articles.title: Jake Paul to face Cedric Doumbe in Christmas Eve boxing comeback, year after suffering broken jaw
articles.summary: Jake Paul's return to boxing will come later this year in a fight against Cedric Doumbé on Dec. 24 in Dubai.
articles.body:
The influencer-turned-boxer will face French combat sports star Cedric Doumbe in his previously announced Christmas Eve comeback fight in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Paul's company, Most Valuable Promotions, announced the news Monday morning. The eight-round cruiserweight bout will take place on Dec. 24 at Coca-Cola Arena.

A broadcast partner for the event has yet to be announced.

Paul (12-2, 7 KOs) returns to the ring for the first time since his sixth-round knockout loss to former two-time world heavyweight champion Anthony Joshua this past December in Miami. Joshua knocked Paul down four times en route to gruesomely breaking his jaw, handing the 29-year-old his second professional defeat and his first loss by knockout.

Paul's injuries required multiple surgeries and a lengthy recovery to address, and even raised questions about his boxing future. Paul admitted on Uncrowned's "The Ariel Helwani Show" in May that he wasn't sure whether he'd ever be able to fight again .

Nearly a year later, though, he's ready to return against Doumbé, who himself returns to boxing after an 11-year hiatus. Doumbé most recently competed in MMA, fighting for PFL and Bellator before stepping away for personal and family matters, Helwani reported. Doumbé greatest success came as a professional kickboxer, where he compiled a record of 75-7-1 and rose to be a two-time GLORY welterweight champion.

Known for his striking prowess and knockout power, Doumbe enters the matchup with extensive combat sports experience, however he's competed only once as a pro boxer, winning a four-round decision over Mohamed Fodil in an April 2015 bout in France.

Doumbé said in a release Monday announcing his participation:

"Jake Paul calls himself the Problem Child, but he's never faced a problem like me. He has no idea what a Frenchman is capable of, and on Thursday, December 24 in Dubai, I'm going to eat 'El Poulet' for dinner. Jake loves to talk, and so do I, but after what Joshua did to his jaw, I'm not sure how much talking he has left. I'm going to finish the job Joshua started. Dubai is a special city to me, and on Christmas Eve, I'll be waving le Tricolore over his unconscious body. France, this one's for you."

Paul's return date was announced on Oct. 29, days before Doumbé was revealed as his next opponent.

Paul said in a press release announcing the fight:

"I've spent years proving people wrong, taking risks, and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I'd face. Nothing that's happened has changed my belief in myself or what I'm working toward. I'm hungrier than ever, and on Thursday, December 24, I'm returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey."

Paul's boxing career began in 2020, with the influencer-turned-fighter winning his first six bouts before losing to Tommy Fury in 2023. Paul went on another six-fight win streak — including a victory over Mike Tyson — before the loss to Joshua, who was the biggest test in his career to that point.

"Jake Paul has spent his career challenging what people think is possible," MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian said in the release. "Twelve months ago he suffered a double broken jaw against a two-time heavyweight world champion and since then many have doubted his desire or need to return to boxing. Well he is back, and that tells you everything about the competitor Jake Paul is and how much he loves this sport."

The planned Christmas Eve event will come just two weeks after Joshua's next fight, a highly anticipated bout against Tyson Fury on Dec. 11.

articles.title: Canelo Alvarez could have 'influenced' referee in Christian Mbilli fight, says promoter Camille Estephan
articles.summary: Canelo Alvarez beat Christian Mbilli by unanimous decision to win back the WBC super-middleweight title in Riyadh; Mbilli docked point in eighth round for hitting the back of the head; Watch Chris Billam-Smith fight Cheavon Clarke on November 7, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Canelo beat Mbilli by unanimous decision in Riyadh on Saturday to reclaim the WBC world super-middleweight title with scores of 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110 in the Mexican superstar's favour.

But in the eighth round, Mbilli's hopes of a late charge were stalled when referee Hector Afu docked a point for hitting on the back of the head after Canelo gestured to the official following an exchange on the ropes.

"Close fight, hats off to Canelo - a great performance," Estephan said.

"As far as the ref, It seemed like he was influenced to take that point off. But I'm not in his shoes. I can't understand what went through his mind.

"Regardless, there will be many more big fights for Christian. He belongs."

Canelo was returning to boxing a year after his stunning loss to Terence Crawford that cost him his undisputed super-middleweight crown and ended his reign as holder of the division's four major titles.

Mbilli was elevated to full WBC champion after Crawford's departure from the division, having previously held ⁠the interim title with his victory over Maciej Sulecki in June 2025.

The 31-year-old Cameroon-born boxer had fought to ​a split draw against Lester Martinez on the undercard of the Alvarez-Crawford showdown, ending ​a run of 29 consecutive professional victories, while the loss now to Cancelo is his first as a professional.

In a post on Instagram, translated from French, Mbilli wrote: "Last night didn't go the way I wanted. I'll learn from this experience, get back in the gym, and come back stronger.

"Thank you to my team and to all of you for your messages of support."

articles.title: Ya es oficial: Jake Paul se enfrentará a Doumbé el 24 de diciembre en Dubái
articles.standfirst: El púgil estadounidense más mediático se vuelve a subir al ring ante una de las mayores superestrellas de los deportes de contacto en Francia
articles.summary: El púgil estadounidense más mediático se vuelve a subir al ring ante una de las mayores superestrellas de los deportes de contacto en Francia
articles.body: Hace unos días, Jake Paul anunció su regreso al ring para el próximo 24 de diciembre en Dubái. Tras ser noqueado por Anthony Joshua hace un año y fracturarse la mandíbula, el influencer y boxeador estadounidense prometía un regreso por todo lo alto, y hoy se ha conocido su rival: Cédric Doumbé. El peleador galo es una de las mayores superestrellas de los deportes de contacto en Francia, y este enfrentamiento se realizará en peso crucero, en lo que se espera que sea un éxito de ventas. Para quien no conozca a Doumbé, hay que destacar que es uno de los mejores kickboxers de la historia. El galo ha fue campeón de kickboxing en peso wélter en GLORY y se convirtió en el peleador con más defensas de la historia de la categoría. También ha sido campeón mundial de K-1 y Full Contact, lo que le ha permitido ser una auténtica eminencia en los deportes de contacto. Por si fuera poco, en 2021 dio el salto a las MMA, y rápidamente acumuló varios K.O. que prometían mucho de su figura. De hecho, hasta Kylian Mbappé acudió a algunos de sus combates. Sin embargo, desde 2024 no se sabe nada de él, y su regreso se esperaba que fuese en MMA dentro de poco, aunque todo ha dado un giro de 180 grados cuando Jake Paul y su equipo le han contactado y le han propuesto este combate. Lo normal es que haya cierta diferencia de tamaño entre Jake Paul y Doumbé, ya que el estadounidense es bastante más grande que el galo. Por tanto, las críticas volverán a salpicar al estadounidense, que después de ser considerado un "weight bully" ante peleadores como Tyron Woodley, Nate Diaz o Ben Askren había decidido medirse a Anthony Joshua para callar a sus críticos. Obviamente la decisión la pagó cara, con una fractura de mandíbula y varios meses apartado del ring, por lo que ha aprendido la lección y ha decidido ir a por rivales un tanto más inexpertos en el boxeo a ver qué tal le va. Porque sí, Doumbé es una eminencia en los deportes de contacto, pero no en el boxeo, donde apenas tiene experiencia. Por tanto, será Paul el que tenga las de ganar en este duelo.

articles.title: John McCarthy: Dan Miragliotta got Renato Moicano call wrong at UFC Vegas 123 — 'It's not fair'
articles.summary: "Big" John McCarthy doesn't agree with Dan Miragliotta's controversial and fight-changing stand-up from UFC Vegas 123 this past Saturday.
articles.body:
"Big" John McCarthy doesn't agree with Dan Miragliotta's controversial fight-changing stand-up from UFC Vegas 123 this past Saturday.

The lightweight main event between veteran mainstay Renato Moicano and rising prospect Tom Nolan was one-way traffic through the first round and a half. Using his superior grappling, Moicano took Nolan's back early and locked in a tight body triangle for most of the fight — until the referee, Miragliotta, unceremoniously stood them up.

Nolan immediately took over with his striking game and ultimately found the third-round stoppage on his rattled opponent.

McCarthy, one of the sport's most tenured officials, explained what was so wrong with Miragliotta's stand-up call on Monday's "The Ariel Helwani Show."

"MMA is a sport where you have all these different disciplines that you're able to utilize," McCarthy told Uncrowned. "It's not something that's supposed to give an advantage to one particular style, whether it be a striking art or a grappling art. It's supposed to be open. When you're taking a look at it, Renato Moicano went out and he was establishing that, 'I want to take the fight to the ground and I want to utilize my grappling skills to get a win,' and he was doing that. He did that throughout the first round; he got the takedown about a minute and a half into it. He kept it and had the figure-four body lock.

"I think Dan looked at that and gave him all the time to work with it. Then, when [the stand-up] happened, somewhere about a minute into the second round, he had that same position — 'was he working,' is the real question here. Many times, we talk about someone who gets a great position — what we call a seatbelt — and just holds on and just doesn't do anything. Obviously we have to tell them that they need to work and try to finish the fight, but we can't ask them to improve their position when it is already the best they can be in."

Stand-ups from ground positions aren't uncommon in MMA. The biggest difference, however, is in this case McCarthy believes Moicano was obviously working and fighting rather than simply stalling without looking to advance position or do damage.

"The punches he was throwing weren't going to knock Tom Nolan out. We know that," McCarthy said. "But they could create that one moment where Nolan made a mistake that led to a rear-naked choke. Our job as officials is supposed to be to be fair to both fighters. I don't care if Renato Moicano or Tom Nolan wins; I care that they both get to perform to the best of their abilities, utilizing the skill sets they have worked so hard to attain, and whoever's skill set is best is the one that should come out on top."

One talking point that's been raised about why Miragliotta may have stood up the fight from such a dominant position has focused whether he was influenced by a restless crowd in the UFC's Meta Apex. Although Moicano was working throughout the grappling sequence, he wasn't necessarily close to finishing the fight yet, as McCarthy noted.

Regardless of the scenario and whether it made the fight less exciting, McCarthy doesn't think that's what happened.

"I think it was a matter of him looking at it and thinking he had already given [Moicano] a whole round and another half of a round without a finish, and then Tom Nolan grabbed ahold of the wrist," McCarthy said. "That was the moment Moicano wasn't being offensive for just a couple of seconds, and [Miragliotta] decided to stand them up.

"The real problem with it is, it's not fair. You gave a great advantage to one fighter over another. You created a disadvantage in the fight for Renato Moicano. He put the fight where he wanted — he had him in a position where he was in a figure four, and with that, it's incumbent upon Tom Nolan to get himself out. It's not for an official to get him out, especially when Moicano is working and trying. Nolan is working and trying, but he has to try to get out, or he's going to be down two rounds.

"You look at it, and it's a matter of what is fair," McCarthy continued. "Many times we'll take positions away from fighters when there's a foul, based upon the fact that we don't want to take a point, but we'll actually take them out of the position as a punishment because that's our way of evening it out. 'You fouled, so I'm going to take you out of the position, and now we're going to be in a stand-up. You're going to lose what you had gained, and that's a way of us actually creating a punishment.'

"There was no reason [to stand them up], in my opinion — and look, I love Dan Miragliotta. He's a great person, I've always gotten along with him, and I think he's been a fantastic referee for the 27 years he's been doing it now. This was just one of those instances. I think he was looking toward giving the judges more to go off of and giving the fans more to see, thinking there wasn't enough going on, when that's not his responsibility."

Moicano, 37, suffered a big setback with the loss after his successful rebound win over Chris Duncan in April. He has three fights left on his UFC contract before he intends to weigh his options in free agency and likely leave MMA behind for boxing.

Nolan, meanwhile, continues to surge, extending his win streak to six in the Octagon.

In Monday's appearance, McCarthy harped on the neutral position debate — of which, Moicano's back position was not — and said he's personally never stood up a fighter from a body triangle in his 30-plus-year career as a referee.

McCarthy used the Charles Oliveira vs. Max Holloway rematch from earlier this year as a comparable example to Nolan vs. Moicano. In that fight, Oliveira largely dominated Holloway in similar positions for significantly longer periods, going the full five rounds.

With that in mind, Miragliotta's mid-fight call creates an even deeper controversy — or potential conspiracy, as McCarthy highlights.

"The UFC doesn't tell officials, 'Hey, you need to stand people up.' That doesn't happen, but there are times when, look, you have to be honest about this. I am not saying that they were in any way influencing anybody in any direction, because they were not. But Renato Moicano is an older fighter, and the truth is that what is better for the business is for Tom Nolan to do well," McCarthy said.

"It's not that they are sitting there doing anything to make this fight happen a certain way, but what works better is for Tom Nolan to win the fight. He is the up-and-coming young fighter that they can do a lot with. So when you look at it after the fact, did the stand-up help Tom Nolan? It absolutely helped Tom Nolan."

Ultimately, it's too late to fix anything now in Nolan and Moicano's cases, and all parties seem to acknowledge that.

"You have to look and understand that Renato knew when he got stood up that he had just been screwed. Now, when I say screwed, I am not saying he is claiming it was inappropriate, but he knows he needs to be on the ground to be successful," McCarthy said. "'I got this fight to the ground, and now you are standing me up, and now I've got to try to survive the stand-up of Tom Nolan, a guy who throws a lot of jump knees and dangerous techniques.'

"He got caught by those things, so now he is not only fighting Tom Nolan; he is fighting himself. In his head, he is thinking, 'I have two guys to worry about here: I have to worry about whether the referee is going to stand me up again if I take him down.' You have to look at all the damage Tom Nolan did in that minute and ask if it had a diminishing effect on Moicano. Of course it did, that is what fighting is. It is being able to do enough damage that diminishes someone's ability to defend themselves to the point where they can't, and that's when the fight ends.

"So, when you look at all the things that happened, you realize they all had an effect on the outcome. With the UFC, I am sure they were happy that Tom Nolan won and thought it was not that bad of a thing, but was it fair? That's my one question."

articles.title: Carlos Adames vs Gerome Warburton: WBC middleweight champion to fight Welshman on November 14 live on Sky Sports
articles.summary: Carlos Adames will fight Gerome Warburton as part of Riyadh Season Zuffa Boxing 13 on November 14, live on Sky Sports; a 10-round bantamweight co-feature will see Jason 'Mayhem' Moloney make his Zuffa Boxing debut against Andres Teran
articles.body:
The pair meet in a 10-round main event of Riyadh Season Zuffa Boxing 13, with the bout to be contested at a contract weight of 165 pounds.

Adames, 25-1-1 (18), returns to action less than eight months after his dominant win over Austin 'Ammo' Williams, the third title defence for the Dominican Republic native, who is unbeaten in his last eight bouts.

Warburton, 18-2-2 (2), reignited his career in 2026, earning back-to-back decision victories over former British middleweight champion Nathan Heaney.

The 31-year-old from Colwyn Bay, Wales, is a former Welsh middleweight champion who has challenged for British and Commonwealth honors.

The 10-round bantamweight co-feature will see Australian former world champion Jason 'Mayhem' Moloney, 29-4 (20), make his Zuffa Boxing debut against Mexico's Andres Teran , 19-2 (14).

Moloney, a consensus world-ranked contender, has won two consecutive bouts in Australia to position himself for another championship run. Teran turned heads at Zuffa Boxing 08 in June, knocking out the previously undefeated Floyd Diaz in the sixth round.

Also fighting on November 14, super-middleweight contender Bruno Surace , two fights since his knockout victory over Jaime Munguia, takes on Poland's unbeaten Kamil Bednarek in a 10-rounder.

In an eight-round tilt featuring unbeaten lightweights, Mexico's Ivan Ortiz will battle Dariial Kuchmenov.

Ortiz upset the previously unbeaten Justin Viloria in his last outing, while Kuchmenov upped his KO streak to five with a fourth-round blitzing of Jorge Lagunas.

Two of Uzbekistan's top emerging talents - heavyweight Jakhongir Zokirov and light heavyweight Tullo Boymatov - return following standout Zuffa Boxing debuts earlier this year.

Plus middleweight contender Radzhab Butaev looks to get back on the winning track against Colombian Alexander Castro in a 10-rounder.

articles.title: 'Put boxers first': Former World Boxing chief's message to warring BFI factions
articles.summary: New Delhi: Former World Boxing president Boris van der Vorst has called on India's boxing administrators to put aside their differences and ensure
articles.body: New Delhi: Former World Boxing president Boris van der Vorst has called on India's boxing administrators to put aside their differences and ensure stability within the Boxing Federation of India (BFI), warning that the sport cannot afford organisational uncertainty with larger focus on Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.With Indian boxing enjoying a successful run on the international stage -- winning 7 medals at the Commonwealth Games and 6 at the Asian Games -- van der Vorst believes the priority should be to protect the progress made rather than allow administrative disagreements to affect the sport's preparations for the next Olympic cycle.In an exclusive interaction with TimesofIndia.com, the former World Boxing chief said India's boxing leadership needed to come together behind the current administration of president Ajay Singh, with the interests of athletes taking precedence over everything else."Everyone needs now to be focused on this Olympic podium mission. That's what everyone needs to come together for, work together and take care that there will be stability and continuity for Indian boxing," van der Vorst told TimesofIndia.com.The crisis has been brewing since October 8, when BFI secretary general Pramod Kumar issued a notice seeking a no-confidence motion against Singh. The motion cited alleged unilateral decision-making, unauthorised constitutional amendments, intimidation of state associations, financial irregularities and administrative overreach. Kumar's faction further claimed that 28 of the federation's 35 affiliated units had backed the move. Singh's camp, however, questioned the legality of the proposed meeting and maintained that the process did not follow the federation's constitution.The dispute escalated, when Singh and Kumar suspended each other. Singh cited alleged financial irregularities, non-cooperation with investigations and misuse of authority in his action against Pramod Kumar. The secretary general subsequently issued a suspension order against the president, pending the outcome of the no-confidence motion. Both sides accused each other of violating the BFI constitution.The proposed October 28 Special General Meeting (SGM) was subsequently put on hold by the Punjab and Haryana High Court until November 13, following a petition filed by Singh.That did not stop the opposition from making its presence felt. On October 28, representatives claiming the support of 28 of BFI's 35 affiliated units and eight of its 13 executive committee members met Union Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) CEO Raghuram Iyer. The faction submitted a memorandum alleging governance lapses and seeking intervention, including the formation of an independent ad-hoc committee and fresh elections.Against this backdrop, van der Vorst believes the focus must shift back to the athletes and the opportunities ahead. He credited Ajay Singh and BFI's Executive Director Col. Arun Malik for the progress made by Indian boxing, pointing to the investment in the high-performance programme and the exposure provided to boxers through international competitions."I think the most important thing is taking good care under the current leadership for the rough talents and diamonds that are already available for many years," he said.Recalling his early visits to India, van der Vorst said he had recognised the potential at grassroots gyms and believed the country could become a boxing powerhouse if the talent was nurtured correctly.He pointed to the depth India now possesses across weight categories, with three or four boxers capable of competing at the highest level in several divisions."You have to thank, of course, the current president Ajay Singh for doing this and also the great team of Col. Arun Malik, who took care of the talents in the high-performance squad," he said.With the Los Angeles Olympics less than two years away and the qualification pathway approaching, van der Vorst said Indian boxing needed continuity in its preparations."It is the responsibility now of all the boxing leaders here in India to look into the mirror and say to yourself, how can we contribute to this important mission and support the leadership of Ajay Singh and Col. Arun Malik," he said."By putting the interest of the boxers first, you take care that the current leadership can do their work," he stated.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ilia Topuria: "Vuelve el Matador"
articles.standfirst: El hispanogeorgiano lanzó un mensaje en sus redes sociales
articles.summary: El hispanogeorgiano lanzó un mensaje en sus redes sociales
articles.body: Han pasado casi siete meses desde la derrota de Ilia Topuria (17-1) en UFC Casa Blanca ante Justin Gaethje (28-5). Siete meses desde aquel 14 de junio en el que el 'Matador' cedió el invicto y la corona del peso ligero. El hispanogeorgiano, que se encuentra desde hace semanas en Georgia, ha vuelto a los entrenamientos... pero todavía se desconoce cuál será la fecha de su próximo combate y a quién se enfrentará. De momento, Topuria ha mandado un nuevo mensaje en redes sociales... confirmando su 'regreso'. Ilia ha estado en el Memorial de la Batalla de Didgori, unos 40 kilómetros la oeste de Tiflis, y desde allí ha compartido el siguiente post. "Volví al lugar donde todo empezó. No para rememorar el pasado, sino para recordar. Vuelve el Matador", escribía. El futuro para Ilia Topuria, mientras, está abierto y ofrece numerosas opciones. Por ahora todo pasa por saber qué hará Justin Gaethje. El actual campeón no ha defendido su corona y se duda que vaya a hacerlo. Una retirada o una especie de superpelea (con nombres como McGregor o Volkanovski bajo los rumores) es lo que se ha planteado. Topuria busca una revancha que le permita recuperar su cinturón de campeón... pero en la fila hay más nombres que también quieren la corona de las 155 libras: Arman Tsarukyan (24-3) y Paddy Pimblett (24-4). Tanto el armenio como el inglés, existiendo con ambos una gran rivalidad, son serias opciones... ya sea en un combate 'eliminatorio' o en una pelea por el título vacante.
